implementation_constraints: Pure Python standard library only: json, re, shlex, sys.
Reads exactly one JSON object from stdin and communicates allow/block by exit code 0/2.
Fails closed for invalid JSON, invalid object shape, malformed shell parsing, or commands that cannot be proven read-only.
Matches the .approved marker as a case-insensitive substring.

unresolved_intent.decision: Recognize a conservative explicit set of read-only tool names: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, List, Find, Search, WebFetch, WebSearch, NotebookRead, after case-insensitive normalization that removes punctuation.
unresolved_intent.rationale: The package names tool families but not host-specific exact names; an explicit allowlist avoids treating arbitrary unknown tools as safe merely because their names contain read-like words.

unresolved_intent.decision: Treat Bash, Sh, Shell, Cmd, PowerShell, Pwsh, Terminal, and Command as shell/command tools.
unresolved_intent.rationale: The package gives Bash as an example and describes a shell/command family; these are common host names for tools that execute command strings and need the same default-deny handling.

unresolved_intent.decision: Allow shell commands naming .approved only when every parsed command segment begins with a known read-only executable and contains no redirection, assignment-like write target, or write/in-place flag.
unresolved_intent.rationale: The package requires proving the whole command read-only but leaves the parser boundary unspecified; segment-wise token analysis is conservative without executing or inspecting the filesystem.

unresolved_intent.decision: For non-shell unknown tools, inspect both dictionary keys and values recursively for the marker, but only string content is marker-bearing.
unresolved_intent.rationale: The acceptance text says the marker appearing anywhere in arguments blocks; keys can carry paths in some tool schemas, while non-string JSON primitives are not filenames or textual arguments.
